info.title: Tracepad API
info.summary: Lightweight, self-hosted, OTLP-native store for LLM and agent traces.
info.description: The read API is the product's contract: the UI, the CLI and the MCP server are thin clients over exactly these endpoints, and a feature that is not here does not exist. Responses are flat snake_case JSON with RFC 3339 timestamps and opaque cursors. Every response spends a byte budget on payloads (default 51200, `?budget=` to override): a payload that does not fit is cut at a UTF-8 boundary and replaced by a truncation marker naming where the whole of it lives.

post.summary: OTLP/HTTP trace ingest, protobuf or JSON
post.description: The canonical OTLP endpoint. Point any OpenTelemetry SDK at it with `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` and an authorization header. Both OTLP encodings are accepted — `application/x-protobuf` and, per `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/json`, `application/json` with the ids hex-encoded as the OTLP specification prescribes. The response mirrors the request's encoding. A 200 means the spans are committed and fsynced.

schema.description: The same message in the OTLP/JSON encoding, optionally gzipped: `traceId`, `spanId`, `parentSpanId` and the ids inside a link are hex, not base64, and 64-bit integers may be strings or numbers

200.description: Accepted; the body is an ExportTraceServiceResponse carrying partial_success when spans were skipped, in the encoding the request arrived in

415.description: Content-Type is neither application/x-protobuf nor application/json

429.description: The write queue is full; retry after the Retry-After delay

post.summary: OTLP ingest under the Langfuse SDK's path
post.description: The same endpoint as `/v1/traces`, at the path a Langfuse SDK sends to. Setting `LANGFUSE_HOST` to a tracepad is the whole migration.

post.summary: Langfuse SDK: an upload URL for one media body, or null when it is already stored
post.description: The first call of the Langfuse SDK's media channel. `mediaId` is the SDK's own derivation — the first 22 characters of the URL-safe base64 SHA-256 — which the SDK checks. `uploadUrl` is null when this project already holds the body, in which case nothing is sent and the named trace's ref is recorded: settled if the project has the trace, and otherwise pending, dated as the bytes rather than the ask, until the trace's spans arrive — so the null answer too counts toward the pending cap and can be a 429; a body only another project holds is still asked for, because the bytes are the proof of possession. Under the `placeholder` setting `uploadUrl` is always null and nothing is kept. The body is read leniently: fields a newer SDK adds are ignored.

sha256Hash.description: The standard base64 SHA-256 of the body

200.description: The id and where to PUT the bytes

uploadUrl.description: A presigned URL, good for an hour and for this server's lifetime; null when nothing needs sending

403.description: The trace was deleted or erased within the hour and is not stored now: no upload is taken for it

429.description: The project has 10,000 uploads waiting for their traces and this one — with an upload URL or without — would be another; `Retry-After: 60`. A trace the project has is never refused

put.summary: Langfuse SDK: the presigned upload of one media body
put.description: Where `uploadUrl` points. Presigned like an object-store URL: the SDK sends no credential here, and the signed `token` names the project, the trace, the hash, the type and the length the upload was granted for. A body that does not match the declared length and SHA-256 — or the `x-amz-checksum-sha256` header when it is sent — is refused and nothing is stored.

403.description: The token is missing, forged, expired, or for another id, and is refused having read nothing; or the key that asked for it has been revoked, or its trace was deleted or erased within the hour, which is decided before the body is read and answered at once, the body then drained up to the length the ask declared and dropped

413.description: The body is larger than the upload declared

429.description: The project has 10,000 uploads waiting for their traces and this one's trace has not arrived; `Retry-After: 60`. Not for the retry of an upload already stored. Decided before the body is read and answered at once, the body then drained up to the length the ask declared and dropped

get.summary: Langfuse SDK: one media body's type, size and address
get.description: The Langfuse shape for a body this project holds. `url` is `GET /api/v1/media/{sha256}`, which needs a credential of the project like every read; it never changes, so `urlExpiry` is a year away.

contentType.description: The type this project stored the body under

uploadedAt.description: When this project's hold of the body began

patch.summary: Langfuse SDK: the report on one media upload
patch.description: The SDK's account of how its PUT went. There is no upload state to keep — the PUT stored the body or it did not — so a failure is logged and every report is answered 204.

get.summary: This endpoint map
get.description: Where an agent that has never seen this API starts: every endpoint with a one-line description, plus the link to this document. Needs no key: it says what the API is, never what is in it.

policy.description: Which kinds of caller the route admits

scope.description: What a project key must hold to be admitted: one of its three scopes, `any` key, or `none` whatever its scopes. Sessions and the admin token never consult it

get.summary: The OpenAPI 3.1 document for this API
Whether this server still needs its first owner
get.description: The one thing the interface can learn without a credential. While it answers `{"required": true}` the server prints a setup link at every start (good for 24 hours) and every other screen but an invitation redirects to `/setup`. `enabled` is false when the server runs with `TRACEPAD_SETUP=off`: no link is printed, `POST /api/v1/setup` refuses, and the first owner is created with the admin token. `expired` is true when setup is needed and on but no link this start printed still works — past its 24 hours, or never minted because an owner could sign in at start; a restart prints a new one.

post.summary: Create the first owner from the token the server printed
post.description: The token is 32 random bytes minted at each start while no enabled owner exists, kept in memory only and printed in the setup link — so a token from a log file yesterday opens nothing today, and a restart is the recovery if the link was lost. Answers 403 to a wrong token and to a second attempt once an owner exists.

password.description: 10 to 72 bytes of UTF-8 — what bcrypt reads; maxLength counts characters, so a password outside plain ASCII meets the 72-byte limit sooner

201.description: The owner, signed in; the session cookie is set

403.description: A wrong or spent token, or an `Origin` that is not this server's

415.description: The body is compressed, or not declared `application/json`: a route that takes no credential takes a plain JSON body

post.summary: Sign in with an email and a password
post.description: A wrong email, a wrong password, a disabled account and one that has never accepted its invitation all answer the same 401 with the same sentence: any difference between them is a way to find out who has an account here. Five failures for one email inside fifteen minutes and the next is a 429 with `Retry-After`.

200.description: The account, signed in; the session cookie is set

403.description: The request carries an `Origin` that is not this server's

415.description: The body is compressed, or not declared `application/json`: a route that takes no credential takes a plain JSON body

post.summary: Set a password from an invitation link and sign in
post.description: The token is single-use and good for seven days. Accepting replaces whatever password the account had — which is what makes one path serve both an invitation and a reset — ends its other sessions, and stamps the login.

password.description: 10 to 72 bytes of UTF-8 — what bcrypt reads; maxLength counts characters, so a password outside plain ASCII meets the 72-byte limit sooner

200.description: The account, signed in; the session cookie is set

403.description: A wrong or spent token, or an `Origin` that is not this server's

415.description: The body is compressed, or not declared `application/json`: a route that takes no credential takes a plain JSON body

post.summary: End this session
post.description: Deletes the row and clears the cookie. A project key or the admin token gets 400: this is a question only a session can ask.

get.summary: The signed-in account and the projects it can reach
get.description: The one call the interface makes on load. The project list rides in it because the shell needs both at once: for an owner it is every live project with the role `owner`, for everyone else their memberships, sorted by name.

200.description: Who is signed in and what they can reach

patch.summary: Change this account's display name, password or preferences
patch.description: A password change needs the current one and signs every other session of the account out, because changing it is what a person does when they think somebody else has it. `preferences` replaces the stored object whole — validated only as a JSON object of at most 16 KiB; the interface owns its shape.

new.description: 10 to 72 bytes of UTF-8 — what bcrypt reads; maxLength counts characters, so a password outside plain ASCII meets the 72-byte limit sooner

preferences.description: Replaces the stored object; `422` for anything but an object, or one over 16 KiB

200.description: The account as it now stands

409.description: The password changed between checking the current one and writing the new one; sign in again

get.summary: This account's sessions, the current one marked
get.description: The reason sessions are rows: "sign out everywhere" is a decision a person makes by looking at the list and recognising which one is the laptop they still have. The id is the row's — sha256 of the cookie — and cannot be turned back into a credential.

delete.summary: End every session of this account but the current one

get.summary: Version, uptime, database size and ingest counters since start
get.description: Self-diagnosis without a metrics stack. The counters are in-memory and cover this process only, which is what `counters.since` says. Row counts and counters are the asking project's own — `payloads` is absent because it cannot be attributed to one, `projects` is how many tenants share this process (naming none of them), and `size_bytes` is the whole deployment's file on disk.

200.description: What this process knows about itself

size_bytes.description: The database file plus its write-ahead log, for the whole deployment

rows.description: Row counts within the asking project, plus `projects` as a bare tenant count

read_slots.description: Reads being served now, for the whole deployment, against TRACEPAD_READ_CONCURRENCY; a read that finds none free waits within its deadline

runs.description: The link between traces and dataset runs, as this project sees it

pinned_traces.description: Traces a live run keeps out of the retention sweep — the size of retention's one exception

orphan_traces.description: Trace deliveries since start that named a run this project does not have; they are stored, and each unknown id is logged once

raw.description: The archive of export bodies: what an export can replay, and what it cannot. Unlike the counters this is on disk, not since start.

enabled.description: Whether accepted bodies are still being kept (TRACEPAD_STORE_RAW)

bytes.description: What the archive occupies on disk, compressed — the number an operator moving `raw_retention_days` is deciding about

traces_before_window.description: Traces whose earliest span started before the oldest batch arrived, and which an export therefore cannot cover. A lower bound: a late export of an old trace lands after the batch line.

media.description: The images and files ingest took out of this project's payloads: the setting that decides whether they are kept, and what the kept ones cost. A body two projects share is in both projects' figures.

count.description: Distinct bodies this project's traces and raw batches point at

compaction.description: The deployment's compaction: after an erasure, a trace deletion or a project's purge, the next sweeper pass merges the search index, drains the freelist and truncates the write-ahead log, so what the deletion unlinked is overwritten rather than left in the file

requested_at.description: The latest request still pending; null when none is

completed_at.description: When one last finished; null before the first

counters.description: This project's ingest traffic, and its reads the read bounds refused, since the process started

reads_timed_out.description: This project's reads the read deadline stopped (TRACEPAD_READ_TIMEOUT)

reads_refused_busy.description: This project's reads refused because no read slot came free before the deadline

get.summary: List traces newest first, filtered and cursor-paginated
get.description: Rows carry the aggregate columns and never a payload — a listing is for choosing what to fetch. To read one trace whole, follow with `GET /api/v1/traces/{id}`; to go straight to the newest match, use `GET /api/v1/traces/last`.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Exact match on the trace's user id

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: Exact match on the trace's session id

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The trace name. A comma-separated list matches **any** of them; items are trimmed, duplicates collapse, an empty item is a 400, repeating the parameter is a 400, at most 100 items, and a name containing a comma is not expressible here. A trace with no name never matches. `GET /api/v1/facets` lists the values in a range with their counts

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Repeatable; a trace must carry every tag given. At most 50 distinct values, duplicates collapsing first; more is a 400 (`tag: at most 50 values`), since a trace keeps at most 50 tags

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `error` keeps traces with at least one failed observation, `ok` keeps the rest

parameters.name: min_cost
parameters.description: Keeps traces whose total cost is at least this much. A trace whose client provided no cost has none and never matches.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated subset of the row fields. An unknown name is a 400.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `?cursor=` for the next page; null on the oldest one

prev_cursor.description: Pass back with `?direction=prev` for the page before; null on the newest one

total.description: Present only with `?count=`: how many rows the filters match, capped at 1000

total_capped.description: Present only with `?count=`: the count stopped at the cap and the real number is larger

delete.summary: Delete every trace a listing filter matches before `to`, in bounded rounds
delete.description: The filters are the trace listing's own, with the same names and the same validation, so "delete what I am looking at" is one call with no second grammar — and `to` is required, dry run and confirmed alike: it closes the set, so that what was previewed is what is deleted however much ingest flows in between. Without `confirm` it answers with the dry run, counting the match exactly rather than at the listing's cap, naming the eval runs that would lose traces, and stating that raw OTLP bodies are not touched. With `confirm` echoing the project's name it deletes at most `limit` of the newest matches, in chunks of one hour — and at most fifty chunks, whichever bound comes first — each chunk its own transaction re-rolling the hours it emptied, and answers whether there is `more`; repeat the same call while there is. A filter matching nothing is a successful dry run of zero and a successful deletion of nothing. Editor role.

parameters.description: Exact match on the trace's user id

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: Exact match on the trace's session id

parameters.name: name
