A trace with no name never matches. `GET /api/v1/facets` lists the values in a range with their counts

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Repeatable; a trace must carry every tag given. At most 50 distinct values, duplicates collapsing first; more is a 400 (`tag: at most 50 values`), since a trace keeps at most 50 tags

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `error` keeps traces with at least one failed observation, `ok` keeps the rest

parameters.name: min_cost
parameters.description: Keeps traces whose total cost is at least this much

parameters.name: confirm
parameters.description: The name of the project whose slice is being destroyed. Without it the endpoint changes nothing and answers with the dry run; a value that does not match is a 400 that also changes nothing.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many traces one confirmed call may delete — one round; the round also ends at fifty one-hour chunks, whichever comes first. Out of range is a 400, not a silent clamp

200.description: What one round deleted and whether there is more, or the dry run of what the filter matches

get.summary: The newest trace matching the filters, whole
get.description: The task shortcut: `?status=error&expand=io` answers "why did the last run fail" in one round trip instead of list, filter, get, and one get per observation. Takes every filter of the listing and returns exactly what `GET /api/v1/traces/{id}` returns.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The trace name, or a comma-separated list matching any of them

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Repeatable; every tag given. At most 50 distinct values

404.description: Nothing matches; the message names the filters that found nothing

get.summary: One trace with its observations as a nested tree
get.description: Children are nested inside their parents, siblings ordered by start time. An observation whose parent has not arrived yet renders at the root with its `parent_observation_id` intact, and so does one that would sit deeper than 100 levels, keeping its own children. A trace past 10,000 observations or 32 MiB of structure is answered with its first observations by start time and `observations_omitted`. Payloads ride only with `?expand=io`.

delete.summary: Delete one trace and everything attached to it
delete.description: The trace, its observations, scores, payloads, search entries and annotation-queue items, with the hour it started in re-rolled in the same transaction. Raw OTLP bodies are not touched: a raw batch holds many traces, and a trace cannot be cut out of one. Without `confirm` it answers with the dry run, naming the eval runs that would lose the trace; with `confirm` echoing the trace id it deletes. An unknown id is a 404 either way. Editor role.

parameters.name: confirm
parameters.description: The id of the trace being destroyed — its only identity. Without it the endpoint changes nothing and answers with the dry run; a value that does not match is a 400 that also changes nothing.

200.description: What was deleted, or the dry run of what would be

get.summary: The whole input, output and metadata of one observation
get.description: The one endpoint no byte budget applies to: it exists to be the `full` target of every truncation marker, and a budget here would recurse. A span id is unique only inside its trace, so pass `?trace_id=` when the same id appears in more than one — every truncation marker already carries the pair.

parameters.name: trace_id
parameters.description: Optional; required only when the span id is ambiguous within the project

409.description: The span id appears in more than one trace; the message lists the candidates

get.summary: One image or file a payload references, by the SHA-256 of its bytes
get.description: Ingest takes images and files out of the payloads and leaves a reference object in their place, `{"tracepad_media": "<sha256>", "mime_type", "size"}` — this is where its bytes are. Served only to a project that points at the body, from a trace or from a raw batch; any other hash is 404, so a hash seen in a log is not a capability across projects. Content-addressed, so cached for a year and immutable. Every body is served under a sandboxing Content-Security-Policy and `nosniff`; anything but an image, audio or video is sent as an attachment.

200.description: The bytes, in the MIME type this project stored them under

get.summary: List the raw export bodies oldest first, cursor-paginated
get.description: The archive: every accepted export, kept as it arrived. This is the one listing here whose natural order is forward, because a replay has to preserve arrival order — a receiver that does not upsert by span id must see the spans in the order the world produced them. Follow with `GET /api/v1/raw/{id}` for a body; `tracepad export --otlp` is these two endpoints in a loop. Both are an editor's read: a project key, an editor or an owner — a viewer session is refused, because the archive is the bulk way out of a project.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: RFC 3339, inclusive, on `received_at`

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: RFC 3339, exclusive, on `received_at`

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Out of range is a 400, not a silent clamp

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Which way to page from the cursor. This listing runs oldest first, so `next` walks towards newer batches and `prev` back towards older ones; with no cursor, `next` is the oldest page and `prev` the newest. Rows come back oldest first either way

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Adds `total` and `total_capped`: how many batches the filters match, counted up to 100000 — high, because this count answers "how much is this export about to send"

get.summary: One raw export body, in the Content-Type it was received in
get.description: The bytes the client posted, gzip already removed. Exempt from the response budget for the reason `/observations/{id}/io` is: a cut body is not a smaller batch, it is a broken one. `X-Tracepad-Received-At` and `X-Tracepad-Dialect` carry what a client needs to name a file or label a manifest without a second request.

X-Tracepad-Dialect.description: Absent when the mapper claimed nothing

X-Tracepad-Scrubbed-At.description: Present when a user-data erasure rewrote the batch: the body is the batch as received minus the erased user's spans

get.summary: List sessions by most recent activity, filtered and cursor-paginated
get.description: Aggregated from the traces that named a session; there is no session table. `from`/`to` bound the *traces*, half-open like the trace listing, so a session appears when any of its traces falls in the window and its totals then describe those traces. To read one session's traces, follow with `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}`.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Exact match on the user id of a session's traces

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `?cursor=` for the next page; null on the oldest one

prev_cursor.description: Pass back with `?direction=prev` for the page before; null on the newest one

total.description: Present only with `?count=`: how many sessions the filters match, capped at 1000

total_capped.description: Present only with `?count=`: the count stopped at the cap

get.summary: One session: its totals and its traces
get.description: A session is not a stored entity but the set of traces that named it. Every aggregate counts traces: `error_count` is how many of the session's traces failed, not how many spans did.

total_cost.description: Absent when no trace of the session carried a cost

get.summary: Counts, errors, cost and latency percentiles per bucket
get.description: `unit` says what a bucket counts: grouping by hour, day, environment, release or total counts traces, and grouping by model counts observations, because a trace has no model. Grouped by release, a trace that named none falls in the bucket with the empty key. Grouped by `total`, the whole window is one bucket under the empty key — the same shape as a day bucket, with percentiles merged over every hour in the window — and it takes every filter the other groupings take. An empty range answers with no buckets rather than with fabricated zero rows. Latency percentiles are histogram-based: accurate to a few percent, and stable across the expiry of the raw rows.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Restricts every bucket to one end user. The shape, the groupings and `unit` are unchanged; a `hour` or `day` timeline, and the `total` bucket, additionally carry `sessions` per bucket. Statistics for one user trail the raw data by the same rollup lag as the rest

total_cost.description: Absent when nothing in the bucket carried a cost

tokens.description: Token sums over the observations in the bucket, on every grouping and both units. Each key is present only when something in the bucket carried that count, and the object is absent when none of the three is — absent, never zero, like `total_cost` — and always absent with `user_id`, whose rollup holds no token sums. Cache-read tokens are the input tokens a provider reported as served from its cache; reasoning and cache-creation counts are not summed

sessions.description: Present only with `user_id` and an `hour`, `day` or `total` grouping: how many of that user's sessions began in this bucket. A session is counted where it starts, so a sum over any range is exact

get.summary: Score means, rates and category shares per bucket, one series per score name
get.description: The quality curve beside the traffic one. A score is counted in the hour of the **trace it names** — not in the hour it was graded — and takes that trace's environment, release and model, so the buckets line up with `GET /api/v1/stats`. A score that names no trace, and a `text` score, are not counted at all. Without `name` every score name in the range is a series; with it, one. `targets` says what was counted: grouping by model counts only the scores that name an observation, because a trace-level score has no model to sit under; every other grouping counts each score once. A numeric series carries `mean`, `min` and `max` per bucket, a boolean series the `rate` of true values, and a categorical series the `categories` seen. Answered from the hourly roll-up behind the watermark and from the raw rows for the tail, so it trails live traffic by the same lag as the statistics.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Only the score filed under this name. Absent, every name in the range comes back as its own series

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many series to return, the busiest score names first. A score name needs no config, so the number of them is unbounded client input; `omitted` says how many this left out

targets.description: `observation` when grouping by model, where only scores naming an observation can be counted; `any` otherwise, where every score counts once

omitted.description: How many score names `limit` left out, rarest first; 0 when every name in the range is here

get.summary: The environments, releases and trace names in a range, each with its trace count
get.description: What the three many-valued filters can be set to, for the range in view: the distinct values of `environment`, `release` and `name` among the traces between `from` and `to`, each with the number of traces carrying it, sorted by count descending and then by value. It answers the range and nothing else — the counts do not respect the other filters, so the list does not change as boxes are ticked. At most 100 values per column; `omitted` says how many were left out, rarest first. A trace with no release is not a release, and a trace with no name is not a name. Answered from the hourly roll-up behind the watermark and from the raw rows for the tail, so a value first seen a minute ago is already here.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: RFC 3339, inclusive. Defaults to the oldest hour the rollup holds, which is also as far back as this endpoint looks: it does not scan the raw traces for hours the rollup no longer covers. A window whose `from` is not before its `to` is a 400

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: RFC 3339, exclusive. Defaults to now

from.description: The start of the range these counts are for

omitted.description: How many values the cap left out of each column; 0 when the list is the whole truth

get.summary: List users by last seen, traffic, cost or errors, cursor-paginated
get.description: Answered from the per-user rollup alone, so it trails the raw data by up to twice the rollup interval: a user first seen minutes ago is not listed yet, and `GET /api/v1/users/{id}` is exact for any id. Every number counts traces, not observations, and `sessions` counts sessions where they started. Sorting is always descending, with ties broken by `user_id`; a user with no costed trace sorts last under `sort=cost`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Which of the four questions this listing is answering: who was here recently, who runs the most, who costs the most, who fails the most

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: Keeps ids starting with this, case-sensitively. A prefix rather than a substring, because an index answers a prefix; the listing is not search

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `?cursor=` for the next page; null on the last one

prev_cursor.description: Pass back with `?direction=prev` for the page before; null on the first one

total.description: Present only with `?count=`: how many users the filters match, capped at 1000

total_capped.description: Present only with `?count=`: the count stopped at the cap

get.summary: One user: traffic, sessions, cost, errors and latency
get.description: The rollup plus the live tail — the traces past the rollup's watermark — so the answer is exact for any id, including one the listing has not caught up with. `404` when neither half has seen it. For this user's activity over time, and the breakdown by environment or model, ask `GET /api/v1/stats?user_id=`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user id, as the application set it

post.summary: Write one score or an array of them
post.description: An array is all-or-nothing: one transaction, and one 400 naming the first invalid item. A 201 means the rows are on disk. No Content-Type is required.

429.description: The write queue is full; retry after the Retry-After delay

get.summary: List scores, filtered and cursor-paginated
Fetch one score

delete.summary: Retract one score; no dry run, a re-POST puts it back
delete.description: A score is one row, so there is no echo to type: writing the same id again recreates it.

get.summary: List prompt names with where their labels point
get.description: Alphabetically by name. `direction` reads towards the start of the alphabet, so both ends of the listing cost what one page costs.

get.summary: Fetch one prompt by version, by label, or the latest
get.description: With neither `version` nor `label`, the highest version. `latest` is a virtual label meaning the same thing; there is no implicit `production`.

delete.summary: Delete a prompt with every version and label; a dry run until `?confirm=` echoes the name
delete.description: The name's whole history goes at once — versions are never deleted alone. Traces that ran the prompt keep the name and version they recorded: that is a string pair the client sent, not a reference into this table. Without `confirm` it answers with the counts and changes nothing.

200.description: What went, or the dry run of what would

post.summary: Append a version to a prompt
post.description: Versions are append-only and numbered inside the write transaction, so parallel creates produce 1..N with no gaps. A name's type is fixed by its first version. `expect_version` makes the append conditional on the name still being where the author left it.

type.description: Required on the first version of a name

prompt.description: A string for a text prompt, an array of {role, content} messages for a chat one

expect_version.description: The version the author believed this name was at — `0` for a name they believe is new. A mismatch is a `409` naming the version it is actually at, and writes nothing. Absent means append to whatever is there.

409.description: `expect_version` disagrees with the name's current state; nothing was written

version.description: The version the name is actually at; 0 when it does not exist

get.summary: List a prompt's versions, newest first
get.description: Without the bodies: a version list is for picking and diffing. `labels` is every label of the name with the version it points at — the whole map, not the part of it that falls on this page.

labels.description: Every label of the name and the version it points at

get.summary: Unified diff between two versions of a prompt
get.description: A unified text patch over the pretty-printed `prompt` and `config` of the two versions — the format every consumer already reads. Empty when the two versions are identical.

put.summary: Point a label at a version
put.description: The deploy path: promote by moving `production` forward, roll back by moving it back. One row, no new version.

200.description: The version the label pointed at

get.summary: List datasets by name, cursor-paginated

put.summary: Create a dataset or replace its description and metadata
put.description: The envelope only: the items and the version clock are untouched. A dataset also comes into being on the first POST of items to its name.

get.summary: One dataset: its version and counts

delete.summary: Delete a dataset with its items and runs; a dry run until `?confirm=` echoes the name
delete.description: The one destructive act here: every version of every item and every run go with the dataset, and the traces the runs were pinning return to the retention window — they are not deleted. Without `confirm` it answers with the counts and changes nothing.

200.description: What went, or the dry run of what would

post.summary: Add or edit items, one or an array, one version tick for the batch
post.description: All or nothing. The dataset's version advances by exactly one if any item in the batch changed and not at all if none did, so re-posting the same cases is idempotent; `changed` says how many produced a row. An item's id is the idempotency key; an edit is a new row of the same id, and the old one stays readable at every earlier version.

version.description: The dataset's version after the write

changed.description: How many items produced a row; 0 leaves `version` where it was

429.description: The write queue is full; retry after the Retry-After delay

get.summary: The items at a version, whole, in first-appearance order
get.description: Budget-exempt: the consumer is the harness, and a truncated test case is a different test case. Bounded by `limit` and by the body cap at write time. Default `version` is the current one; a version above it is a 400.

version.description: The version the items were resolved at

get.summary: One item as of a version

delete.summary: Archive an item at a new version
delete.description: Nothing is destroyed: the item is gone from the current version and still there at every earlier one. A 404 when the item is unknown or already archived at the current version.

200.description: The version the archive landed on

get.summary: Every row of one item's history, newest first
get.description: Archived rows included, each flagged: an edit is a row and a delete is a row.

post.summary: Open a run over the dataset at its current or a named version
post.description: The run pins the dataset version the harness must fetch its items at, and the response carries it. A client-supplied `id` makes the call retry-safe: a known id answers 200 with the existing run unchanged. The store never executes anything — the harness stamps `tracepad.run_id` and `tracepad.item_id` on the spans it exports, and closes the run with `/finish`.

metadata.description: What was being tried, in the harness's own terms

dataset_version.description: The version to pin; the current one when absent, and a 400 above it

200.description: The run that already had this id

get.summary: List a dataset's runs newest first, cursor-paginated
List the project's runs newest first, filtered by dataset and status, cursor-paginated
get.description: Every dataset's runs in one listing, ordered by `(created_at, id)` like the per-dataset one and paged by the same cursor shape. The rows are the run objects without `summary`: a page of runs is for choosing one. `?count=` adds the capped total the filters match.

parameters.name: dataset
parameters.description: Exact dataset name; a name outside the grammar is a 400

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Keeps the runs in one state

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `?cursor=` for the next page; null on the oldest one

prev_cursor.description: Pass back with `?direction=prev` for the page before; null on the newest one

total.description: Present only with `?count=`: how many runs the filters match, capped at 1000

total_capped.description: Present only with `?count=`: the count stopped at the cap

get.summary: One run with its summary
get.description: The run object with `summary`: how much of the dataset it covered, what its traffic cost, what its scores came to, and which models and prompts it actually ran. The listing leaves the summary out.

delete.summary: Delete a run, releasing its traces to the retention window
delete.description: One row of bookkeeping. The traces it held are not deleted; they stop being pinned and live as long as retention says.

released_traces.description: How many traces the run was keeping out of the sweep

get.summary: The run's items with the attempts it made at each
get.description: The items of the run's dataset version in first-appearance order, each with the traces of the run that answered it. `output` is the trace's root observation's output; `expected_output` and `output` are budgeted and cut with a marker naming where the whole payload lives. `?unknown=true` appends the run's traces that no item of its version accounts for.

parameters.name: unknown
parameters.description: `true` appends the traces whose item is not in the run's dataset version, after the known items

get.summary: Two runs of one dataset side by side
get.description: Per score name: each run's aggregate, the delta between the means, and how many items improved, regressed or stayed — `improved` and `regressed` only for names whose config gives a direction, `changed` for the rest. Then the items, paginated, each with its per-name pair and verdict. Equality is exact. Runs of different datasets, and a run against itself, are a 400.

post.summary: Close a run as finished, or as failed with a reason
post.description: The store never infers completion: a run stays `running` until the harness says otherwise. A run closed twice is a 409. Linking does not stop at finish — a late span of a trace that started inside the run still belongs to it.

get.summary: List score configs by name
get.description: Whole, not paged: a project declares a handful of names.

put.summary: Create or replace the config that binds a score name
put.description: Declarative: the whole config, every time, and a re-PUT of the same body is a no-op. From then on a score posted under this name must have the config's `data_type`, a numeric value inside `min`/`max`, a categorical value among `categories`; a violating score fails its batch with a 400 naming it. Scores already stored are never re-validated.

get.summary: One score config

delete.summary: Remove a score config; the scores it admitted stay

get.summary: List the annotation queues with their progress
get.description: Whole, in name order, with no paging: a project has as many review programmes as somebody named. Each carries the score configs a reviewer must fill and the counts of what is pending, completed and skipped.

put.summary: Create an annotation queue or replace it whole
put.description: Declarative, like a score config: the body is the queue, and a re-PUT of the same body writes nothing and answers 200. Every name in `score_configs` must already exist, or the call is a 400 naming the missing one. Changing the list later governs the items not yet completed; nothing re-validates what is already done.

description.description: What this queue is for, as its author wrote it

score_configs.description: The score names a reviewer must set on every item, in the order the desk asks for them. Each must be a declared score config, and no name twice.

200.description: The queue was replaced, or the body said what it already said

get.summary: One queue: its score configs and its counts

delete.summary: Delete a queue with its items; a dry run until `?confirm=` echoes the name
delete.description: The list goes and the scores written while annotating stay: they are attached to the trace, not to the queue. Without `confirm` it answers with the count and changes nothing.

200.description: What went, or the dry run of what would

post.summary: Add one target or an array of them; a target already queued counts as existing
post.description: All or nothing, and idempotent: a trace or observation the queue already holds comes back as the item it already is, whatever its status, so a retried script does not double the queue. The target need not exist yet — an item may be queued for a trace whose spans are still in flight.

201.description: The items the targets resolve to

ids.description: In input order, the id of each target's item — the one just added or the one already there

get.summary: The queue's items oldest first, filtered and cursor-paginated
get.description: In `seq` order — the order they were added is the order they are worked in — and paging both ways like every other listing.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Keeps items in one state. A spelling outside the list is a 400

parameters.name: annotator
parameters.description: Keeps the items this name has: the ones it completed or skipped, and the pending ones it is holding a claim on. `completed_by` is empty on a pending item, so matching it alone would answer "nothing open" for somebody who is working through the queue

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `?cursor=` for the next page; null on the last one

prev_cursor.description: Pass back with `?direction=prev` for the page before; null on the first one

total.description: Present only with `?count=`: how many items the filters match, capped at 1000

total_capped.description: Present only with `?count=`: the count stopped at the cap

post.summary: Add the newest traces a listing filter matches, capped by `limit`
post.description: The filters are the trace listing's own, with the same names and the same validation, so "queue what I am looking at" is one call with no second grammar. The newest `limit` matches are added as trace items; `capped` says more matched than were taken, and a second call with `to=` set at the oldest added continues. With no filter at all it takes the newest `limit` traces of the project.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Exact match on the trace's user id

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: Exact match on the trace's session id

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The trace name. A comma-separated list matches **any** of them; items are trimmed, duplicates collapse, an empty item is a 400, repeating the parameter is a 400, at most 100 items, and a name containing a comma is not expressible here. A trace with no name never matches. `GET /api/v1/facets` lists the values in a range with their counts

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Repeatable; a trace must carry every tag given. At most 50 distinct values, duplicates collapsing first; more is a 400 (`tag: at most 50 values`), since a trace keeps at most 50 tags

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `error` keeps traces with at least one failed observation, `ok` keeps the rest

parameters.name: min_cost
parameters.description: Keeps traces whose total cost is at least this much

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many traces this call may add. Out of range is a 400, not a silent clamp

201.description: What the filter matched and what was added

matched.description: How many traces the filter matches, counted exactly

capped.description: More matched than `limit` allowed; the rest are still waiting

get.summary: The next item to annotate, claimed for ten minutes
get.description: Hands out the annotator's own unexpired claim if they have one — a reload must not hand a reviewer a different trace mid-verdict — and otherwise the oldest pending item nobody holds, claiming it for ten minutes. The window is a constant, not a setting. `item` is null when nothing is claimable, and `pending` then counts what other people are holding. Any completion, skip or reopen clears the claim; reading an item does not take one.

parameters.name: annotator
parameters.description: Who is asking. Written to `claimed_by`, and to `completed_by` when they finish

200.description: The item to work on, or nothing to work on

pending.description: Pending items in the queue, other people's claims included

get.summary: One item
get.description: A read, and only a read: it takes no claim.

delete.summary: Remove one item from the queue
delete.description: No dry run and no echo: a re-add recreates the row, and the scores it was about were never in this table.

post.summary: Mark an item done; refused unless every score the queue asks for is on its target
post.description: The queue promised a shape, and *completed* means the shape was filled — checked here, against the scores actually stored, whoever wrote them: a judge's verdict already on the trace counts, which is what lets a reviewer confirm one rather than repeat it. A trace item needs scores that name no observation, and an observation item scores that name its own. A 409 carries `missing` with the names that are not there; a second completion is a 409 naming who got there first.

409.description: A score the queue asks for is missing, or somebody else completed it first

missing.description: The score config names with no score on the target

post.summary: Mark an item skipped, with the reason
post.description: Not every trace deserves a verdict, and the reason is what makes that readable on the queue page afterwards. The claim is released. A *completed* item is refused with a 409 naming who completed it: a skip writes the same columns a completion filled, so it would destroy the record rather than add to it — reopen it first.

reason.description: Why it was skipped; shown on the queue page

post.summary: Return a completed or skipped item to pending
post.description: For the manager who disagrees with a verdict or wants a skip looked at again. An item that is already pending is not refused: what reopening does to it is release the claim, which is what the desk's *Later* asks for. The scores stay where they are — reopening asks for another look, not for a retraction.

get.summary: Every account with its standing and its projects
get.description: The page an owner opens to answer "who can see what", so the projects and roles are on the row rather than behind a click. Sorted by email.

post.summary: Invite an account; the link is shown once
post.description: Creates an account with no password and the single-use link that sets one, good for seven days. The link is in this response and in no other, ever — only its hash is stored — and carrying it to the person is the owner's job: there is no mail here. A token that sets a password means the password never passes through the owner's hands.

owner.description: An owner has every project, so `memberships` must then be empty

201.description: The account and its invitation link

get.summary: One account with its projects

patch.summary: Change an account's name, owner standing or disabled flag
patch.description: The last enabled owner cannot be demoted or disabled: 409. Making somebody an owner drops their memberships, because an owner has every project. Disabling ends the account's sessions at once.

200.description: The account as it now stands

delete.summary: Delete an account; a dry run until `?confirm=` echoes its email
delete.description: For people who are gone. It takes their memberships, sessions and invitations and nothing else: a score does not name its author, and the keys it minted keep working, listed in the dry run. Disabling is the reversible way to take access away today.

200.description: The dry run: what would go, and the email that makes it happen

post.summary: Mint a fresh invitation link; this is also the password reset
post.description: Ends the account's sessions and voids any earlier link. The old password goes on working until the new link is used, so an owner cannot lock somebody out by pressing this: the failure mode of a reset is somebody locked out on a Friday.

put.summary: Give an account a role in a project
put.description: An owner already has every project, so a membership for one is a 409.

delete.summary: Take a project away from an account
delete.description: Removing a membership that is not there is not an error: the state the caller asked for is the state that holds.

204.description: The account no longer has this project

get.summary: List projects
get.description: The admin token sees every project; a project key sees its own and nothing else, with `key` on the row saying which key asked and what it may do — any key may call this, whatever its scopes.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: `deleted` adds soft-deleted projects with their purge dates. Admin token only.

parameters.name: activity
parameters.description: `24h` puts `traces_24h` on every row: the traces of the last 24 hours, counted the way `GET /api/v1/stats` counts them (spec 029 #8). Any other value is a 400.

200.description: The projects the caller may see

post.summary: Create a project and its first key pair
post.description: The secret key is in this response and in no other: only its hash is stored. A name inside another project's grace window is a 409 naming the restorable one.

201.description: The project and its one-time secret

get.summary: One project with its retention windows
get.description: A soft-deleted project's own key still reaches this one, so that a caller about to restore can see what it is restoring and until when. Any key may call this, whatever its scopes, and a key's answer carries `key`: which key asked and what it may do.

patch.summary: Rename a project or move its retention windows
patch.description: Renaming needs the admin token; the windows are the project's own business. `null` means keep forever. A window that shrinks is destructive: without `confirm` it answers with the preview, and it applies only when `confirm` echoes the project's name.

retention_days.description: How long a trace is kept after it arrived; null keeps it forever. Bounded because a window becomes a nanosecond cutoff, and a large enough one would overflow into the future and match every row — "forever" is null, not a big number.

raw_retention_days.description: The window for stored OTLP bodies; null follows retention_days

stats_retention_days.description: The window for the hourly statistics rollup, measured by the hour a row summarizes; null keeps it forever, which is the default. The rollup outlives the traces it summarizes, so shortening this window destroys history the trace sweep spares — it asks for the same confirmation the other two do.

media.description: What ingest does with an image or file it takes out of a payload: `store` keeps the body, `placeholder` keeps only a reference saying it was not stored. Not destructive either way — bodies already kept stay until their traces go.

200.description: The project as it is now, or the dry run of a window that shrinks

delete.summary: Soft-delete a project, restorable for seven days
delete.description: The keys stop authenticating immediately and the project vanishes from listings; the data is destroyed by the sweeper after a fixed seven-day grace. Admin token only, even for one's own project. Without `confirm` it answers with the preview.

200.description: The dry run: what deleting it would eventually destroy

202.description: Deleted, with the date the data is purged

post.summary: Undo a soft delete inside its grace window
post.description: No confirmation: it destroys nothing. Reachable with the project's own key even while deleted, so that a deployment without an admin token can still undo one.

get.summary: List a project's keys, who minted each and when it was last used
get.description: An owner or editor signed in, or the admin token; a project key is answered 403, because no key lists, mints or revokes keys. The secrets are not here because they are not anywhere: only their hashes are stored.

post.summary: Mint a key pair; the secret is shown once
post.description: An owner or editor signed in, or the admin token; a project key is answered 403. Several active pairs are what makes rotation zero-downtime: create the new one, move the SDKs, revoke the old. The body says what the key may do, which never changes afterwards: to narrow or widen a key, mint another and revoke it. The key records who minted it.

scopes.description: What the key may do: `ingest` sends spans, uses the Langfuse media channel and writes scores; `read` is every read of the project's data; `write` is every change a key may make. Any non-empty combination; duplicates collapse. Missing, empty or an unknown word is a 400

name.description: Which program holds the key. Trimmed; at most 64 characters; no control or bidirectional control characters (422); not unique

201.description: The new pair, secret included this once

delete.description: An owner or editor signed in, or the admin token; a project key is answered 403. Revoking a project's last key, or the last one that carries `ingest`, stops its ingest, so that one is a dry run until `confirm` echoes the project's name.

200.description: The key is gone, or the dry run for the last one or the last with `ingest`

delete.summary: Erase everything stored about one user
delete.description: Erases, synchronously, everything the store holds about the traces filed under the user id: the traces, their observations, payloads and scores, the annotation-queue items pointing at them (`annotation_items`), the session-only scores of the sessions they carried (`session_scores`), every version of the dataset items cut from them (`dataset_items`, with the datasets named under `affected_datasets`), and their spans inside the raw OTLP bodies — each batch that held one is rewritten without it and marked `scrubbed_at`, or deleted when nothing else was in it (`raw_spans`, `raw_batches_rewritten`, `raw_batches_deleted`). The preview's `raw` block counts the batches the erasure will read and those older than the trace window, which nothing can attribute any more. The answer's `compaction` says when the sweeper pass that overwrites what was unlinked is due, and `pre_migration_backup`, while one exists, names the backup the erasure does not rewrite and the day it goes. Without `confirm` it answers with the preview; the echo here is the user id.

200.description: What was erased, or the dry run of what would be

get.summary: Who has a role in this project; owners are not listed
get.description: The project side of the question an owner asks from the account side at `/api/v1/accounts`. Owners are absent because they are not membership rows — the screen says "and every owner" rather than pretending they are.

bearerKey.description: A project's secret key, `tp-sk-…`. A key holds one or more of three scopes — `ingest`, `read`, `write` — and every operation names the one it asks of a key as `x-tracepad-scope` (`any` for every key, `none` for no key). A key without it is answered 403 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="<needed>"` and a body naming the scopes it holds and the one the route needs

basicKeys.description: `base64(public key:secret key)`, the shape a Langfuse SDK sends

adminToken.description: `TRACEPAD_ADMIN_TOKEN`, sent in the same header as a project key. Required for everything cross-project, for creating and deleting a project, and for the account routes; beside an owner's or editor's session, it is what lists, mints and revokes a project's keys, which no project key does — which is what makes it the recovery when every owner's password is lost. A server with none configured answers 403 and says so.

sessionCookie.name: tracepad_session
sessionCookie.description: A browser session: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` over TLS, set by the three ways in and lasting `TRACEPAD_SESSION_DAYS` (default 30), sliding. On a route whose policy is `member` or `editor` a session must also name the project it is asking about with `X-Tracepad-Project`, and an unsafe method must carry an `Origin` (or `Referer`) whose host is the request's `Host`, the first value of `X-Forwarded-Host`, or the host of `TRACEPAD_URL`.

From.name: from
From.description: RFC 3339, inclusive. The range is half-open, so walking a timeline never reports a row twice.

Environment.name: environment
Environment.description: The environment a trace ran in. A comma-separated list matches **any** of them: `?environment=production,staging`. Items are trimmed and duplicates collapse; an empty item (`a,,b`, `a,`) is a 400, as an empty value is, and so is repeating the parameter — one list, one parameter. At most 100 items; beyond that, a 400. An environment whose name contains a comma is not expressible here. `GET /api/v1/facets` lists the values in a range with their counts

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Out of range is a 400, not a silent clamp

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: The opaque `next_cursor` or `prev_cursor` of a previous page

Direction.name: direction
Direction.description: Which way to page from the cursor. With no cursor, `next` is the newest page and `prev` the oldest — both ends are a direction rather than an offset. Rows come back newest first either way

Count.name: count
Count.description: Adds `total` and `total_capped`: how many rows the filters match, counted up to 1000. Off by default, because the count changes with the filters and not with the page

Search.name: q
Search.description: Full-text search over one field of one observation — input, output, metadata, name or status message — or over the trace name. Words (all must occur), `"quoted phrases"`, `prefix*`. Words, not substrings: `error` does not find `errors`, `err*` finds both. Case and diacritics are folded, identifiers split on punctuation, and only the first 64 KiB of each payload is indexed. A `q` with no word in it is a 400

Release.name: release
Release.description: The deployment the trace ran in, from `langfuse.release` or the resource's `service.version`. A comma-separated list matches **any** of them; items are trimmed, duplicates collapse, an empty item is a 400, repeating the parameter is a 400, at most 100 items, and a release whose name contains a comma is not expressible here. `GET /api/v1/facets` lists the values in a range with their counts

Version.name: version
Version.description: Exact match on the version of the trace's own logic, from `langfuse.version` or `tracepad.trace.version`

ObservationType.name: type
ObservationType.description: Keeps traces with at least one observation of this kind. Exact: `generation` does not match `embedding`. A value outside the list is a 400

Prompt.name: prompt
Prompt.description: `name` or `name@version`: keeps traces with at least one observation that ran this prompt, at any version or at that one. A version is a run of digits after the last `@` with a name in front of it; every other string is a name, `@` included — `@acme/support`, `team@acme/answer`, `name@latest` and `svc@-1` all filter as names. A label is not a version

RunFilter.name: run_id
RunFilter.description: Keeps the traces of one dataset run. A value of another shape is a 400: the ingest mapper claims nothing else into the column, so it could only match nothing

ItemFilter.name: item_id
ItemFilter.description: Keeps the attempts at one dataset item, across runs unless `run_id` narrows it

Expand.name: expand
Expand.description: `io` inlines each observation's input, output and metadata, each cut to an equal share of the remaining budget with a truncation marker naming the rest

Budget.name: budget
Budget.description: Byte budget for the payloads of this response; the structure is never truncated

ConfirmEmail.name: confirm
ConfirmEmail.description: The email of the account being deleted — the one thing about an account a person means. Without it the endpoint changes nothing and answers with a preview; a value that does not match is a 400 that also changes nothing.

Confirm.name: confirm
Confirm.description: The name of the project — or the id of the user — being destroyed. Without it the endpoint changes nothing and answers with a preview; a value that does not match is a 400 that also changes nothing.

ConfirmName.name: confirm
ConfirmName.description: The name of the dataset being destroyed. Without it the endpoint changes nothing and answers with the counts; a value that does not match is a 400 that also changes nothing.

ConfirmPromptName.name: confirm
ConfirmPromptName.description: The name of the prompt being destroyed. Without it the endpoint changes nothing and answers with the counts; a value that does not match is a 400 that also changes nothing.

DatasetName.name: name
DatasetName.description: The prompt-name grammar: one URL path segment

DatasetVersion.name: version
DatasetVersion.description: The dataset version to resolve the items at; the current one when absent. Above the current version it is a 400. A run's `dataset_version` is what to pass here

QueueName.name: name
QueueName.description: The prompt-name grammar: one URL path segment

ConfirmQueueName.name: confirm
ConfirmQueueName.description: The name of the queue being destroyed. Without it the endpoint changes nothing and answers with the count; a value that does not match is a 400 that also changes nothing.

ScoreConfigName.name: name
ScoreConfigName.description: A score name: any name a score may carry can have a config

BadRequest.description: The request cannot mean what it says: an unknown query parameter, a malformed value, a limit out of range

Unauthorized.description: The credentials do not resolve to a project

ServiceUnavailable.description: The credentials could not be checked right now, more passwords were being checked at once than the server allows, or a write met a database condition that passes (a full disk, a lock that did not clear), or a read found no free read slot before its deadline (`the server is busy; retry shortly`): retry after `Retry-After`. A read the deadline stopped while it ran (`the read took longer than 20s and was stopped; narrow the time range or the filters`, the number being `TRACEPAD_READ_TIMEOUT`) carries no `Retry-After`: the same request would be stopped again, so narrow it

NotFound.description: No such thing in this project

Forbidden.description: The credentials are good but do not reach this far: an owner account or the admin token is needed, the role in this project is too low, a project key lacks the scope the operation names in `x-tracepad-scope`, or a cookie request came from another origin

WWW-Authenticate.description: Only when a project key lacks a scope: `Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="<needed>"` (RFC 6750 §3.1)

Conflict.description: The stored state already answers differently: a name that is taken, a project that is already deleted, the last owner being demoted

Unprocessable.description: The request is well formed and the values are not: an email that is not one, a password outside 10-72 bytes, a name over 200 characters

Error.description: The one error shape the whole surface uses

Account.description: A person who signs in, as they see themselves. The email is the sign-in name and nothing else: it is never verified and never written to.

name.description: A display name, which may be empty

owner.description: An owner has every project and every management action, including the accounts themselves

preferences.description: How the interface is arranged for this person: an opaque JSON object the interface owns the shape of, `{}` until written, at most 16 KiB, replaced whole by `PATCH /auth/me`. The dashboard keeps its block order under `dashboard`, keyed by project id

allOf.description: An owner's view of somebody: the standing fields and the memberships.

disabled.description: Access taken away reversibly; the sessions ended when it was set

pending.description: Invited and not yet accepted, so there is no password and no way in yet

last_login_at.description: null means this account has never signed in

projects.description: The membership rows, which are empty for an owner: the flag is the membership

Membership.description: One project an account can reach, with the role it has there

role.description: `owner` is not a stored membership: it is what every project reports for an account with the owner flag

MembershipRow.description: A membership as the endpoint that writes one answers

Me.description: Who is signed in and what they can reach, which is everything the interface's shell needs on load

projects.description: Sorted by name. For an owner, every live project with the role `owner`; for everyone else, their memberships. Soft-deleted projects are not on it.

AccountSession.description: One browser's sign-in. The id is sha256 of the cookie's value and cannot be turned back into one.

current.description: The session this request was made with

Invitation.description: A new account and the link that sets its password. The link is here and in no other response, ever.

AccountDeletion.description: What deleting an account would take, and the email that makes it happen

keys.description: The keys the account minted that still exist, in every project. Not in `would_delete`: deleting the account leaves them working

confirm.description: The exact string `?confirm=` must carry: the account's email

TraceRow.description: A trace as it appears in a listing: aggregates only, never a payload. A field the trace never carried is absent rather than empty.

release.description: The deployment the trace ran in, from `langfuse.release` or the resource's `service.version`

version.description: The version of the trace's own logic, from `langfuse.version` or `tracepad.trace.version`

run_id.description: The dataset run this trace belongs to, from `tracepad.run_id`; absent on ordinary traffic. No foreign key stands behind it: a trace may name a run the project does not have

item_id.description: The dataset item this trace answered, from `tracepad.item_id`; never present without `run_id`

timestamp.description: When the earliest observation of the trace started

total_cost.description: Summed over the observations whose client provided cost; absent when none did

ttft_ms.description: The wait before the first token: the earliest completion start among the trace's observations, minus the trace's own start. Absent when no observation carried one, and negative when a client's completion start precedes its span

Match.description: Where the search hit, present only with `?q=`: the observation and field with the best score among the trace's hits, and a window of the text around the first term. Hits are not marked up — a client that highlights folds the query terms the way the tokenizer does.

observation_id.description: The observation that matched; null when the trace's own name did

snippet.description: At most 160 characters, cut on word boundaries

SessionRow.description: The roll-up over the traces of one session. Every number counts traces, not observations: `error_count` is how many of the session's traces failed.

id.description: The session id, as the application set it

total_cost.description: Summed over the traces that carried a cost; absent when none did

UserRow.description: The roll-up over one end user's traffic. Every number counts traces, not observations: `error_count` is how many of the user's traces failed. `first_seen` and `last_seen` are rounded down to the hour the rollup keeps, except on `GET /api/v1/users/{id}`, where the live tail makes them exact to the second.

user_id.description: The user id, as the application set it

total_cost.description: Summed over the traces that carried a cost; absent when none did

sessions.description: How many sessions of this user have begun. A session with no user id on its traces belongs to no user and is not counted here

first_seen.description: The start of the earliest hour the rollup still holds for this user; it moves forward as `stats_retention_days` sweeps

FacetValue.description: One value a filter can be set to, and how many traces of the range carry it

value.description: The value, exactly as `?environment=`, `?release=` or `?name=` takes it

count.description: How many traces of the range carry it

ScoreSeries.description: One score name over the asked buckets. A name graded two ways — numerically here, categorically there — is two series with the same name, told apart by `data_type`.

data_type.description: Which of the three summaries each bucket carries. `text` scores have nothing to add up and are never a series

ScoreBucket.description: One group of one series. `count` is how many scores fell in it; the rest depends on the series' `data_type` — `mean`/`min`/`max` for numeric, `rate` for boolean, `categories` for categorical. A bucket with no scores does not exist rather than reporting zero.

key.description: The hour, day, environment, release or model this bucket is

count.description: How many scores fell in this bucket

mean.description: Numeric series only: the mean of the values in this bucket

min.description: Numeric series only: the smallest value in this bucket

max.description: Numeric series only: the largest value in this bucket

rate.description: Boolean series only: the share of scores in this bucket whose value is 1, between 0 and 1

categories.description: Categorical series only: how many scores in this bucket carried each value seen. The counts sum to `count`. Only the twenty busiest values of the range are named; the rest are summed under `other`, so the sum still holds — and a series that really has a category called `other` merges with them

RawBatch.description: One archived export body, described. The bytes themselves are at `GET /api/v1/raw/{id}`.

id.description: The batch's id; the path segment of the body endpoint

received_at.description: When the server accepted it, which is the order a replay preserves

dialect.description: Which attribute vocabulary the mapper recognised in it; empty when it claimed nothing

content_type.description: The media type the body is in, which is what a replay posts it under. Batches stored before schema 0012 read as `application/x-protobuf`.

content_encoding.description: How the client compressed it on the wire, for provenance. The stored body is decoded, so a replay does not have to unwrap two layers.

size_bytes.description: The decoded length — what a fetch of the body returns — and not the compressed length the row occupies

scrubbed_at.description: When a user-data erasure rewrote the batch without the erased user's spans; null for a batch as received

observations_omitted.description: Present only when the tree is a part of the trace: `observation_count` minus the observations rendered. A tree holds the longest prefix of the trace's observations, in start-time order, of at most 10,000 observations and 32 MiB of their own fields; an observation whose parent was left out renders at the root with its `parent_observation_id`

Observation.description: One span. `children` holds the spans that named it as their parent and is absent for a leaf.

parent_observation_id.description: The observation this one ran under, whenever it named one. Nested children carry it too; an observation whose parent is not in this trace renders at the root and still carries it.

type.description: What kind of step this was. A span whose client named no type is classified: a model attribute makes it a generation, a zero-duration childless span an event, anything else a span

completion_start_time.description: When the first token came back, as the client reported it — stored uncorrected, so it may precede `start_time`

ttft_ms.description: `completion_start_time` minus `start_time`; absent when either is missing

input_bytes.description: The uncompressed size of `input`, present whether or not the payload itself is inlined

PromptLink.description: The prompt the client said this observation ran. Recorded as sent and resolved against no registry — the store may not manage this prompt at all, and a label that points at nothing is still a label. Absent when the client named none.

version.description: Null when the client named a prompt without a whole-number version

Expansion.description: Present only when `?expand=io` was refused: a trace with more payloads than the budget can carry markers for gets none of them and this instead. Nothing is unreachable — the tree lists every observation id — and `budget_needed` is what to retry `?budget=` with.

payloads.description: How many payloads the trace holds.

budget_needed.description: The budget that would carry a marker for each of them. Never clamped to the maximum, so it may exceed what `?budget=` accepts.

retryable.description: Whether `budget_needed` is a budget this server would accept. False means no budget can carry this many markers — read the payloads one at a time instead.

Truncation.description: A payload too large for this response's budget. `full` is the URL that returns it whole; `trace_id` and `observation_id` are the same target for a consumer that speaks tools rather than URLs.

size.description: The payload's full size in bytes

preview.description: A prefix of the payload, cut on a UTF-8 boundary

ScoreInput.description: One judgement. A score needs a trace or a session, and either a `value` or a `string_value`.

id.description: Generated when absent; writing the same id again replaces the score

data_type.description: Inferred when absent: a `value` makes it numeric, a `string_value` makes it text

timestamp.description: Event time; defaults to receive time

prompt.description: Stored and returned verbatim; interpolation is the client's job

Project.description: A project with its retention windows. `deleted_at` and `purge_at` are present only while a soft delete is inside its grace window.

retention_days.description: null means the data is kept forever, which is the default

stats_retention_days.description: The window for the statistics rollup, which outlives the traces it summarizes; null means it is kept forever, which is the default

media.description: What ingest does with an image or file it takes out of a payload (spec 041 #6)

purge_at.description: When the sweeper destroys the data; seven days after the delete, and not configurable

role.description: Present only when a session asked: what this account may do in this project. A project key and the admin token get no role, because a role is what an account has (spec 028 #12)

traces_24h.description: Present on every row of a listing asked with `activity=24h`, and absent otherwise: the traces whose timestamp falls in the last 24 hours, from the hourly roll-up behind the watermark and the raw rows past it. A soft-deleted project carries 0 (spec 029 #8)

key.description: Present only when a project key asked: which key it is and what it may do, so that a program that met a 403 can learn what it holds

NewKey.description: A freshly minted key pair. The secret appears here and nowhere else, ever.

Key.description: One of a project's keys: the public half, what it may do, who minted it and when it was last used

name.description: Which program holds it; empty when the minter gave none

last_used_at.description: The last request the key authenticated, admitted or refused, written once a minute: a use in the last minute may be missing after a crash. null until the key is used

KeyScopes.description: What the key may do, in this order: `ingest` (send spans, the Langfuse media channel, write scores), `read` (every read of the project's data), `write` (every change a key may make). A key that predates scopes, and a key the server made by itself, holds all three. Fetching one prompt is open to every key, whatever its scopes

KeyMinter.description: Who minted a key. `account`: an owner or editor signed in; `admin_token`: the admin token; `startup`: the server itself, for the first-start project or one `TRACEPAD_PROJECTS` declares; `unknown`: the key predates the record

account_id.description: `account` only, and only while the account exists

email.description: `account` only: the email the account had when it minted the key, kept after the account is deleted

standing.description: `account` only: the minter's relation to the project now. `removed` has no role here any more

AnnotationQueue.description: One review programme: a named list of traces or observations and the score names a reviewer must set on each of them (spec 024).

score_configs.description: The score names a reviewer must fill, in the order the desk asks for them. A name whose config was deleted since stays here: the queue keeps asking for it, and a PUT is how to drop it

QueueTarget.description: What an add names: one trace, or one observation of it. Neither id is looked up — an item may be queued for a trace still in flight — but both are checked for shape, because nothing else can ever be a trace of this store.

observation_id.description: Absent means the item is the trace itself

AnnotationItem.description: One trace, or one observation of a trace, waiting for a verdict. A field it has nothing to say about is absent rather than empty.

observation_id.description: Absent when the item is the trace itself

seq.description: Its place in the queue, monotonic per queue and never reused

claimed_by.description: Who `next` handed it to; absent when nothing holds it

claimed_until.description: When the claim expires and the item is claimable again

QueueDeletion.description: What deleting a queue takes: its items, and nothing else. `confirm` and `note` are present on the dry run only; `deleted` on the confirmed answer only.

confirm.description: Send this back as `?confirm=` to make it happen

DryRun.description: What a destructive request would do, which is what it does until it is confirmed

matched.description: Trace deletion by filter only: how many traces the filter matches, counted exactly

oldest.description: Arrival of the oldest affected row; absent when nothing is affected

affected_runs.description: User-data erasure and trace deletion only: the dataset runs that would lose traces to it, because both override the pin a run puts on them

traces.description: How many of the run's traces this erasure would take

affected_datasets.description: User-data erasure only: the datasets that would lose items cut from the user's traces, every version of each

items.description: How many of the dataset's items this erasure would take

raw.description: User-data erasure only: the raw archive's side of it

batches_to_scan.description: The batches received inside the user's traces' arrival windows, which the erasure decodes; a count, not a decode

unattributable_batches.description: The batches older than the trace window: they may hold spans of traces the sweep already took, and nothing names their user

confirm.description: Send this back as `?confirm=` to make it happen

pre_migration_backup.description: User-data erasure only, and only while a backup exists

Compaction.description: The compaction this deletion asked for: the sweeper pass that overwrites what it unlinked. Both null when it deleted nothing and so asked for nothing.

expected_by.description: When the pass that runs it is due: the next one, or the one after a pass already under way; never earlier than the answer

PreMigrationBackup.description: The newest copy of the database the server wrote before an upgrade, which an erasure does not rewrite, and when the sweeper removes it

remove_after.description: Seven days after `created_at`; the first sweeper pass after it removes the file — not before, and not while the server is down

Deletion.description: What a confirmed destructive request actually removed

pre_migration_backup.description: User-data erasure only, and only while a backup exists

deleted.description: `traces`, `observations`, `scores`, `payloads`, `annotation_items`, and the `media` bodies the project stopped holding with their `media_bytes`

TracesDeletion.description: What one round of a deletion by filter removed

deleted.description: `traces`, `observations`, `scores`, `payloads` and `annotation_items`, summed over the round's chunks

more.description: Traces matching the filter remain; repeat the same call

Dataset.description: A named, versioned set of test cases. `version` advances by one on every write that changes the item set; `item_count` is the live items at that version.

DatasetItemInput.description: One test case. The three bodies are opaque JSON the store never reads inside; the source pair is a note about where the case came from, not a reference.

id.description: Generated when absent; the same id again is an edit of the same item

DatasetItem.description: One item as of a version. `version` is the dataset version the row was written at, which may be earlier than the version it was read at; `seq` is the item's place in the listing, fixed at its first appearance. `archived` appears on the history listing only.

Run.description: A run of a dataset: the container the harness opened, the version it pinned, and how it ended. `finished_at` is null while it is running.

RunSummary.description: How the run went, computed at read time: a run keeps taking late spans, and a stored summary would be wrong in exactly the window somebody is watching.

items.description: Coverage of the dataset at the run's version. `unknown` counts the run's traces that no item of that version accounts for — a harness that ran newer cases, a mistyped id, or a trace that named a run and no item.

traces.description: The run's traffic. `error_count` counts traces that failed, not observations; percentiles are exact over the run's traces, not the bucketed ones of `/stats`.

attempts_max.description: The largest number of traces one item got

total_cost.description: Null when no attempt carried a cost

scores.description: One entry per score name the run carried. `mean`/`min`/`max` for numeric and boolean names, `distribution` for categorical ones, and `count` alone for text.

models.description: Derived from the run's observations, not from what the harness declared

data_type.description: The type the run's scores under this name actually used — the commonest one when they used more than a single type. A config declares what is accepted next and never re-types what is stored, so this can differ from `GET /score-configs/{name}`.

direction.description: From the name's config, and only for a numeric or boolean `data_type`, the two that have an axis; null otherwise, which is what makes a comparison say `changed` rather than `improved`

RunItems.description: The run's items with their attempts, in first-appearance order.

RunItem.description: One case and the attempts the run made at it. An unknown row — a trace whose item is not in the run's version — carries `unknown: true`, no `seq` and no case body; a trace that named no item at all has a null `id`.

RunAttempt.description: One trace of the run: what it cost, how it went, what its root observation answered and how it was scored.

output.description: The trace's root observation's output — the earliest starting observation with no parent — or null when it carried none

RunComparison.description: Two runs of one dataset side by side. `same_version` is false when the dataset moved between them, and the items outside the intersection are labelled rather than dropped.

metadata.description: Only the metadata keys the two runs disagree about, both values

traces.description: Both runs' traffic, and the cost delta

delta.description: b minus a; null when either side carried no cost

ComparedSide.description: One run's aggregate for a score name: the mean for a numeric or boolean name, the distribution for a categorical one, the count alone for text.

ComparedScore.description: One score name across both runs. A name with a direction reports `improved`/`regressed`/`same`; one without reports `changed`/`same`, because without a direction there is no better.

a.description: Null when that run never carried the name

delta.description: b's mean minus a's; null unless both are numbers

ComparedItem.description: One case in both runs. `in` says which side had it: `both`, `a` or `b` when the item is in both versions, and `only_in_version_a` / `only_in_version_b` when the dataset moved between the runs.

scores.description: Per score name both runs scored: the two values, the delta for numbers, and the verdict

DatasetDeletion.description: What deleting a dataset takes: its live items, its runs, and the traces those runs were pinning — which are released, not deleted. `confirm` is present on the dry run only.

confirm.description: Send this back as `?confirm=` to make it happen

PromptDeletion.description: What deleting a prompt name takes: every version of it and every label pointing into it. `confirm` and `note` are present on the dry run only; `deleted` on the confirmed answer only.

confirm.description: Send this back as `?confirm=` to make it happen

ScoreConfigInput.description: What a score name means. `direction` is required for numeric and boolean names and forbidden for categorical and text ones; `min`/`max` are numeric only, with `min` at most `max`; `categories` is required for categorical names and forbidden otherwise.

direction.description: Which way is better; `none` for a number that is typed and bounded but not judged
